source.source_summary: Fully original relationship drama about discovering that a long-term partner maintained an active dating profile to collect matches as an ego boost.

selected.title: My Friend Matched With My Boyfriend
selected.hook: My best friend sent me a screenshot of my boyfriend's dating profile.
selected.voiceover:
My best friend sent me a screenshot of my boyfriend's dating profile. It said he was looking for something casual.

We'd been together for almost four years. Same apartment, shared dog, his toothbrush next to mine. So I assumed somebody had stolen his photos.

Then she showed me the match.

His profile had a picture from a concert we'd attended three weeks earlier. I was cropped out of it.

I didn't confront him immediately. I asked my friend to send one message: "Still single?"

He replied, "Technically, yeah."

That night I put the screenshot on our kitchen table.

He didn't deny it. Instead, he said he'd never met anyone from the app. He only swiped when he was bored because getting matches made him feel attractive.

Then he showed me his messages like that proved his point.

Most conversations were short. No dates, no explicit photos, nothing physical.

But he'd been telling women he was single for eight months. One message even said he lived with a roommate.

Apparently, that roommate was me.

He keeps saying I can't call it cheating because he never touched anybody.

Maybe he's right about the physical part. But every match required him to erase our relationship first.

I packed a bag and stayed with my sister.

Now he wants couples therapy because, according to him, he only wanted attention, not another girlfriend.

Would that distinction matter to you, or is pretending to be single already the betrayal?
selected.youtube_description:
Her best friend matched with the boyfriend she'd been living with for years, and his dating profile included a photo taken only weeks earlier. He insists he never met anyone and only used the app for attention, but his messages raise a harder question about what counts as cheating when someone repeatedly presents themselves as single.
